learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 13 people and locked it in for guaranteed shared birth month.
observations.exploration: Placed one person in each of twelve months; occupied months were disabled until all twelve were filled. At twelve the screen said person 13 must share; placed person 13 in January. Start over reset placements to zero after reveal.
observations.reveal: Confirmed prediction and distinguished twelve people possibly all different from thirteen necessarily sharing. Named the pigeonhole principle and certainty from counting.
observations.visual: Actual 1257 by 936 dark screenshots inspected. Numbered people in a twelve-tile calendar made the boundary visible; January highlighted two people. Reveal readable.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner explicitly excluded learning history and analytics saves.
observations.blinding: No code, metadata or other reviewer judgments read.

prediction.reason: Concrete familiar threshold with a clear certainty question.

interaction.reason: Placement demonstrates the extremal arrangement but mostly requires a prescribed sequence.
interaction.evidence: Occupied months disabled until all twelve filled; thirteen forced a duplicate.

payoff.reason: Explanation directly connects the constructed boundary to a general counting proof.
payoff.evidence: Twelve can avoid sharing; thirteen cannot.

clarity.reason: Familiar month tiles and numbered tokens reduce representation burden.
clarity.evidence: Distinct counts for people seated and months used.

transfer.reason: General principle named without a different application.

accessibility.evidence: Initial AX briefly exposed blank choices, later full labels appeared; screenshots guided selection.

surprise.reason: Certainty without birthdays is a modest counting surprise.

visualExplanation.reason: The full calendar makes lack of a new category visible.

playfulness.reason: Simple seating interaction is tangible but repetitive.

practicalValue.reason: Useful counting lens without an applied follow-up.

depth.reason: Shows a clean boundary and elementary proof.

complexity.reason: Only counting and familiar month categories required.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish possible sharing from guaranteed sharing.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Thirteen placements and a reset; repeated but straightforward.

whyCool: A full calendar proves a guarantee without knowing a single actual birthday.
caveat: Interaction forces the no-duplicate arrangement until the final person; no fresh application tests transfer.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
